"It is by names that these words
have order and track."
This is what it means.
Deeply examine the grand meaning of the title "King."
Within it, there are five categories:
Imperial category (Huáng Kē), Square category (Fāng Kē), Correcting category (Kuāng Kē), Yellow category (Huáng Kē), Going category (Wǎng Kē).
Combining these five categories into one word, we call it "King."
"King" means imperial (huáng),
"King" means square (fāng),
"King" means correcting (kuāng),
"King" means yellow (huáng),
"King" means going (wǎng).

Then the Dao cannot be upright and square;
If the Dao cannot be upright and square,

If virtue cannot correct and circulate universally,

If beauty cannot be radiant,
Then the four directions cannot go (towards it);
If the four directions cannot go (towards it),
Then it is not complete for the king.
Therefore, it is said:
Heaven covers without bounds,
Earth bears with all-embracing love,
The wind carries out commands and unifies its authority,

This is what is meant by the art of kingship.
Deeply examine the great meaning of the title of ruler,
Within it, there are also five categories:
*Yuán kē*, *Yuán kē*, *Quán kē*, *Wēn kē*, *Qún kē*.
Combine these five categories and call them "ruler" in one word.
A ruler is *Yuán*,
A ruler is *Yuán*,
A ruler is *Quán*,
A ruler is *Wēn*,
A ruler is *Qún*.

Then action will lose its foundation;

what is done will not be established,

it will abandon itself,

using power in change,

Names are born from truth,

The meaning of name is truth.

If you want to discern crookedness and straightness,

Those who argue to the extreme,

The king carries out Heaven's will,
taking the perfection of the people's nature as his responsibility.
Now, to examine their true substance and say that the people's nature is already good,
is to lose Heaven's will and abandon the king's responsibility.
If the nature of the myriad people were already good,
then what responsibility would the king have upon receiving his mandate?
It posits that the people cannot be set aright,
therefore it abandons a weighty responsibility and violates a great command;
it is not lawful speech.
In the diction of the *Spring and Autumn Annals*,
matters within that depend on outside factors,
are spoken of from the perspective of the outside.
Now, the nature of the myriad people,
must rely on external teachings before it can become good;
goodness ought to be associated with teaching,
and not with nature.
Associating it with nature leads to many complications and a lack of precision,
resulting in self-achievement and the absence of sages;
this is the mistaken pronouncement of the elders of this world,
and not the art of phrasing in the *Spring and Autumn Annals*.
Unlawful speech, unverifiable claims,
are what the superior man excludes,
so what are we to do with them!
Someone might say:
"Nature has the beginnings of goodness,
the heart has the substance of goodness,
Is Shang An not good?"
He replied,
"No.
Cocoons have silk,
but cocoons are not silk;
eggs have chicks,
but eggs are not chicks.
Making comparisons like this is natural,
what doubt is there?"
Heaven gives the people the Six Classics,
those who speak about human nature should not differ.
However, some say that human nature is good,
and others say that human nature is not yet good,
so what they call good,
each has a different meaning.
Human nature has a beginning of goodness,
causing one to love their parents,
being better than birds and beasts,
then it is called good.
This is what Mèngzǐ said.
Following the Three Cardinal Guides and the Five Constant Virtues,
understanding the principles of the Eight Virtues,
being loyal and trustworthy and loving broadly,
being sincere and kind and fond of propriety,
only then can one be called good.
This is the goodness of a sage.
Therefore, Kǒngzǐ said:
"A truly good person,
I cannot manage to see him;
managing to see someone who is constant is acceptable."
From this perspective,
what the sage calls good
is not easily attainable;
it is not called good merely because it is better than birds and beasts.
If moving its beginning is better than birds and beasts, then it can be called good,
why would good not be seen?
That being better than birds and beasts does not achieve goodness,
is like knowing plants and trees without being called knowing.
The nature of the myriad people is better than birds and beasts but is not called good;
the name of knowing is then taken from the sage.
What the sage decrees,
the world regards as correct;
those who correct morning and evening look to the North Star,
those who correct doubts and suspicions look to the sage.
The sage considers that in a world without kings,
people without teaching
cannot achieve goodness.
Goodness is so difficult to achieve,
and to say that the nature of the myriad people can all achieve it
is wrong.
If based on the nature of birds and beasts,
then the nature of the myriad people is good;
if based on the goodness of human morality,
then the people's nature does not reach it.
To grant that the nature of the myriad people is better than that of birds and beasts,
but do not grant what the sage considers good,
My way of discussing the nature and fate of man differs from Mèngzǐ's.
Mèngzǐ bases his discussion on what birds and beasts do,
therefore he says that human nature is already good.
I base my discussion on what sages consider good,
therefore I say that human nature is not yet good.
Goodness surpasses nature,
sages surpass goodness.
The *Chūnqiū* regards origins as important,
therefore it is careful in rectifying names.
Names are not what originates [from within],
so how can one say that it is "not yet good" or "already good"?
*On Real Nature, Chapter Thirty-Six*
Kǒngzǐ said:
"If names are not correct,
then words are not in accordance [with the truth]."
Now, to say that human nature is already good,
isn't that close to saying that there is no need for teaching and that we should simply let it be natural?
Moreover, it is not in accordance with the way of governance.
Furthermore, names are the substance of nature,
and substance is the essence of nature.
In a time without teaching,
how can it suddenly be good?
Goodness is like rice,
nature is like grain.
Although grain produces rice,
grain cannot be called rice.
Although nature produces goodness,
And the nature (xìng) cannot yet be called good.
Rice (mǐ) and goodness (shàn),
are things that people continue from Heaven (tiān) and complete externally,
not things contained within what Heaven does.
What Heaven does
has a limit to where it reaches and stops.
What's within that limit is called Heaven (tiān),
what's outside that limit is called the teachings of the King (wáng jiào).
The teachings of the King (wáng jiào) are external to the nature (xìng),
and the nature (xìng) has no choice but to follow them.
Therefore it is said:
The nature (xìng) has the resources for goodness (shàn zī),
but is not yet capable of being good (wèi néng wéi shàn).
It's not that I'm using beautiful words,
but that's how it really is.
What Heaven (tiān) does,
stops at cocoon-hemp and grain.
Turning hemp into cloth,
turning cocoons into silk,
turning rice into food,
turning nature (xìng) into goodness (shàn),
all of these are things that sages continue from Heaven (jì tiān) and advance further,
not things that the plain and simple essence of emotions (qíng xìng zhì pǔ) can achieve.
Therefore, they cannot be called nature (xìng).
Those who regulate the morning and evening look to the North Star,
those who resolve doubts and suspicions look to the sages.
What the sages call right,
the world takes as right.
Jīn àn shèngrén yán zhōng, Now, according to the words of the sages,
běn wú xìng shàn míng, originally there was no term like "nature is good,"
ér yǒu shànrén, but there were good people.
Wú bùdé jiàn zhī yǐ. I have not been able to see them.
Shǐ wànmín zhī xìng jiē yǐ néng shàn, If the nature of all people were already capable of goodness,
shànrén zhě héwéi bùjiàn yě? why would good people not be seen?
Guān Kǒngzǐ yán cǐ zhī yì, Observing the intention of Kǒngzǐ in saying this,
yǐwéi shàn nán dāng shèn. I think that goodness is very difficult to achieve.
Ér Mèngzǐ yǐwéi wànmín xìng jiē néng dāng zhī, But Mèngzǐ thought that the nature of all people is capable of achieving it,
guò yǐ. which is excessive.
Shèngrén zhī xìng, The nature of sages,
bù kěyǐ míng xìng, cannot be called "nature,"
dǒushāo zhī xìng, the nature of petty men,
yòu bù kěyǐ míng xìng, also cannot be called "nature,"
míng xìng zhě, zhōngmín zhī xìng. What is called "nature" is the nature of ordinary people.
Zhōngmín zhī xìng, rú jiǎn rú luǎn. The nature of ordinary people is like a cocoon or an egg.
Luǎn dài fù èrshí rì ér hòu néng wéi chú; An egg waits to be brooded for twenty days before it can become a chick;
jiǎn dài cāo yǐ guàntāng ér hòu néng wéi sī, a cocoon waits to be reeled with boiling water before it can become silk,
xìng dài jiàn yú jiàoxùn ér hòu néng wéi shàn. nature waits to be gradually influenced by teaching and instruction before it can become good.
Shàn, jiàoxùn zhī suǒ rán yě, Goodness is what teaching and instruction make it,
fēi zhìpǔ zhī suǒ néng zhì yě, and is not something that can be achieved by simple unadornment.
Gù bù wèi xìng. Therefore, it is not called "nature."
Xìng zhě, yí zhī míng yǐ, What is called "nature" ought to be understood,
wú suǒ dài ér qǐ, as arising without waiting for anything,
shēng ér suǒ zìyǒu yě; and as something that is naturally possessed from birth.
Shàn suǒ zìyǒu, If goodness were naturally possessed,
zé jiàoxùn yǐ fēi xìng yě. then teaching and instruction would no longer be part of nature.
Shìyǐ mǐ chū yú sù, Therefore, rice comes from millet,
And millet cannot be called rice;
jade comes from rough stone,
but rough stone cannot be called jade;
goodness comes from nature,
but nature cannot be called goodness.
This comparison is often considered true for things,
but thought to be untrue for nature.
Why is it not consistent across categories?
The nature of an egg cannot yet create a chick,
the nature of a cocoon cannot yet create silk,
the nature of hemp cannot yet create thread,
the nature of millet cannot yet create rice.
The *Spring and Autumn Annals* distinguishes things by principle in order to rectify their names.
Naming things must each be based on their reality,
the reality of their meaning,
the reality of their essence,
and then they are named.
Naming a falling stone, one postpones the "five,"
to name a reverse flight, one prioritizes the "six,"
these are all their realities.
Sages do not compromise on words, that's all.
"Nature" is the unadorned essence of heaven,
"goodness" is the transformation of kingly instruction.
Without the essence,
then kingly instruction cannot transform;
without kingly instruction,
then the unadorned essence cannot become good.
To have essence without considering good nature,
If the name is not correct,
then it should not be accepted.
"The Dukes, Chapter Thirty-Seven"
It begets, nurtures, and grows;
having achieved, it renews life;
having ended, it begins again.
Its actions, by which the people are benefited and made alive, never cease.
Though Heaven does not speak,
its intention to provide abundantly can be seen.
The sages of antiquity saw Heaven's kindness towards humankind,
so they faced south and ruled the world,
necessarily doing so with universal benefit.
Because the distant cannot be seen by the eye,
and the hidden cannot be heard by the ear,
therefore, beyond a thousand miles,
land was divided and the people separated,
and states were established and rulers appointed,
to have them, on behalf of the Son of Heaven, see what could not be seen,
and hear what could not be heard.
Those who came to court were summoned and questioned.
The term "dukes" (zhūhóu) still means "multiple protectors."
"Discourse on the Five Elements, Chapter Thirty-Eight"
The King Xiàn of Héjiān asked Master Dǒng of Wēnchéng, saying:
"The Classic of Filial Piety (Xiàojīng) says:
'Filial piety is the standard (jīng) of Heaven,
and the righteousness (yì) of Earth.'
What does that mean?"
The reply was:
"Heaven has the Five Elements:
wood, fire, earth, metal, and water.
Wood generates fire,
fire generates earth,
earth generates metal,
metal generates water.
Water is winter,
metal is autumn,
earth is late summer,
fire is summer,
wood is spring.
Spring governs birth,
summer governs growth,
late summer governs nourishment,
autumn governs harvest,
winter governs storage.
Storage is what winter accomplishes.
Therefore, what the father generates,
the son grows;
what the father grows,
the son nourishes;
what the father nourishes,
the son completes.
All that the fathers do,
the sons all respectfully continue and carry on,
daring not to be unlike the father's intentions,
To fully embody the Way of being human.
Therefore, the Five Elements are the Five Elements.
From this perspective,
the father bestows,
the son receives,
and this is the Way of Heaven.
Therefore, it is said:
'Filial piety is the warp of Heaven.'
This is what it means."
The King (Wáng) said:
"Excellent!
The warp of Heaven has already been heard,
I wish to hear the meaning of Earth."
He replied:
"Earth produces clouds and makes rain,
it raises vapors to make wind.
Wind and rain are what the Earth does,
but the Earth does not dare to claim credit for them,
it must attribute them to Heaven.
If they originate from the weather of Heaven,
then they are called Heavenly wind and Heavenly rain;
one does not say Earthly wind and Earthly rain.
Diligence and labor are on Earth,
but the credit always goes to Heaven.
If one is not supremely righteous,
who could do this?
Therefore, those below serve those above,
as Earth serves Heaven;
Kěwèi dà zhōng yǐ. [Can be called great loyalty.]
Tǔ zhě, huǒ zhī zǐ yě. [Earth is the son of fire.]
Wǔxíng mò guì yú tǔ, [Among the five elements, none is more esteemed than earth,]
tǔ zhī yú sìshí wú suǒ mìng zhě, [earth, in relation to the four seasons, has no exclusive domain,]
bù yǔ huǒ fēn gōngmíng. [does not share credit and fame with fire.]
Mù míng chūn, [Wood is named spring,]
huǒ míng xià, [fire is named summer,]
jīn míng qiū, [metal is named autumn,]
shuǐ míng dōng. [water is named winter.]
Zhōngchén zhī yì, [The righteousness of a loyal minister,]
xiàozǐ zhī xíng, [the conduct of a filial son,]
qǔ zhī tǔ. [are taken from earth.]
Tǔ zhě, wǔxíng zuì guì zhě yě, [Earth is the most esteemed of the five elements,]
qí yì bù kěyǐ jiā yǐ. [its righteousness cannot be surpassed.]
Wǔshēng mò guì yú gōng, [Among the five notes, none is more esteemed than gōng (the first note of the pentatonic scale),]
wǔwèi mò měi yú gān, [among the five flavors, none is more pleasing than sweet,]
wǔsè mò guì yú huáng, [among the five colors, none is more esteemed than yellow,]
cǐ wèi 'xiào zhě, dì zhī yì yě.' " [this is what is meant by "filial piety is the righteousness of earth."]
Wáng yuē: [The king said:]
"Shàn zāi!" ["Excellent!"]
Yīfú róngmào zhě, [Clothing and appearance,]
suǒyǐ shuō mù yě; [are what pleases the eyes;]
shēngyán yìngduì zhě, [voice and speech in response,]
suǒyǐ shuō ěr yě; [are what pleases the ears;]
hǎo wù qù jiù zhě, [likes and dislikes, leaving and approaching,]
suǒyǐ shuō xīn yě. [are what pleases the heart.]
Gù jūnzǐ yīfú zhōng ér róngmào gōng, [Therefore, if a gentleman's clothing is proper and his appearance is respectful,]
Then the eyes are pleased;
if the speech is principled,
and the responses are humble,
then the ears are pleased;
if one loves kindness and hates shallowness,
approaches good people and stays away from the eccentric and vulgar,
then the heart is pleased.
Therefore, it is said:
"One's conduct is enjoyable,
and one's appearance is admirable."
This is what it means.

Luxuriant Dew of the Spring and Autumn Annals, Chapter 11
"Being a Person is Heaven, Forty-First"
Being born does not guarantee being a person;
being a person is due to Heaven.
The humanity of a person is rooted in Heaven.
Heaven is also a person's great-grandfather.
This is why people are ultimately similar to Heaven.
A person's physical form
is transformed by Heaven's numbers and completed.
A person's blood and qi
are transformed by Heaven's will and become benevolence.
A person's virtue and conduct
are transformed by Heaven's principles and become righteousness.
People's likes and dislikes
transform into the warmth and coolness of Heaven;
people's joy and anger
transform into the cold and heat of Heaven;
people's acceptance of fate
transforms into the four seasons of Heaven.
Human life has responses of joy, anger, sorrow, and pleasure,
which are like spring, autumn, winter, and summer.
Joy is the response to spring,
anger is the response to autumn,
pleasure is the response to summer,
sorrow is the response to winter.
Heaven's support rests upon people.
The emotions and nature of people have origins in Heaven.
Therefore, it is called "receiving" (受),
because it is a designation from Heaven.
To be a ruler of men,
no path is clearer than to reflect upon the Heaven within oneself,
as if Heaven were producing it.
If he causes this to emerge,
responding to Heaven's production of the four seasons and faithfully carrying out his received mandate,
then the governance of Yáo and Shùn could not be surpassed.
In this case, people can be given life or death,
but cannot be made to rebel.
Therefore, it is said:
"If it is not the Way, do not act;
if it is not the law, do not speak."
This is what is meant by that.
The *Zhuan*
says: Only the Son of Heaven (Tiānzǐ) receives his mandate from Heaven;
all under Heaven receive their mandate from the Son of Heaven;
and a single state receives its mandate from its ruler.
If the ruler's commands are in accordance (with the Way),
then the people will have obedience to commands;
if the ruler's commands are contrary (to the Way),
then the people will have opposition to commands.
Therefore it is said:
"If one person has good fortune,
the ten thousand people rely on it."
This is what it means.
The *Zhuan* says:
Government has three essential elements:
If fathers and sons are not affectionate,
then cultivate their love and kindness;
if high officials are not harmonious,
then respectfully guide them with ritual propriety;
if the common people are not at peace,
then strive to (promote) filial piety and fraternal duty among them.
Filial piety and fraternal duty are the means by which to pacify the common people;
"strive" means to earnestly practice them,
and to transform (the people) through one's own person.
The cycles of Heaven and Earth
cannot solely rely on cold and heat to complete a year;
there must necessarily be spring, summer, autumn, and winter.
The Way of the Sage
cannot solely rely on power and authority to establish governance;
it must have education and transformation.
Therefore it is said:
"Lead them with universal love,
teach them benevolence;"
"What is difficult to obtain,
the noble person does not value,
teach them righteousness."
"Even the Son of Heaven must have those he respects,
teach them filial piety;
he must have those he puts first,
teach them fraternal respect."
This is why power and authority alone are insufficient to rely on,
and the merit of education and transformation is not great!
The "Commentary" says:
"Heaven gives birth to them,
Earth carries them,
the sage teaches them."
The ruler is the heart of the people,
the people are the body of the ruler.
What the heart desires,
the body will certainly find comfort in;
what the ruler desires,
the people will certainly follow.
Therefore, rulers of the people
value filial piety and fraternal respect and love propriety and righteousness,
Zhòng rén lián ér qīng cái lì, [Place importance on benevolence and integrity, and regard wealth and profit lightly,]
gōng qīn zhí cǐ yú shàng ér wàn mín tīng, [when superiors personally and diligently practice this, the myriad people will listen,]
shēng shàn yú xià yǐ. [and goodness will arise among those below.]
Gù yuē: [Therefore, it is said:]
"Xiān wáng jiàn jiào zhī kěyǐ huà mín yě." ["The former kings understood that teaching could transform the people."]
Cǐ zhī wèi yě. [This is what it means.]

Gù wǔxíng zhě, Therefore, the Five Elements,
nǎi xiàozǐ zhōngchén zhī xíng yě. are in fact the conduct of filial sons and loyal ministers.
Wǔxíng zhī wèi yán yóu wǔxíng yú? Is the term "Five Elements" truly like the Five Elements?
Shì gù yǐ dé cí yě. Therefore, it is possible to obtain words.
Shèngrén zhī zhī, The sage knows this,
gù duō qí ài ér shǎo yán, therefore increases his love and decreases his severity,
hòu yǎng shēng ér jǐn sòngzhōng, generously nourishes the living and carefully sees off the dead,
jiù tiān zhī zhì yě. conforming to the regulations of Heaven.
Yǐ zǐ ér yíng chéng yǎng, Using the son to welcome maturity and nourishment,
如火之樂木也。 Like fire that delights in wood.
喪父， The loss of a father,
如水之剋金也； Is like water overcoming metal;
事君， Serving one's lord,

可謂有行人矣。 One can be said to have the proper conduct.
五行之隨， The following of the Five Elements,

五行之官， The offices of the Five Elements,

是故木居東方而主春氣， Therefore, wood resides in the east and governs the spring's qi,
火居南方而主夏氣， Fire resides in the south and governs the summer's qi,

使人必以其序， Employing people must be in accordance with their order,

天之數也。 This is the way of Heaven.
土居中央， Earth resides in the center,

Correctness cannot be established
just as sourness, saltiness, bitterness, and pungency cannot form a taste without sweetness and richness.

Among the great offices of man,
that which does not name what is managed,

among the great offices of Heaven,

"Yang is Honored, Yin is Base, Chapter Forty-three"
The great number of Heaven concludes with ten periods.
Periods are between Heaven and Earth,
completed with ten;
the merit of the periods of growth,
is completed with ten.
Ten is where the number of Heaven stops.
The ancient sages took what the number of Heaven stopped at to be the reckoning of numbers.
Ten is like a renewal,
and the people transmit it generation after generation,
but do not know to examine its origin.
Knowing and examining where it originates,
then one sees where the Mandate of Heaven (tiān shù) begins.
Seeing where the Mandate of Heaven begins,
then one knows where nobility, baseness, adversity, and obedience lie.
Knowing where nobility, baseness, adversity, and obedience lie,
then the emotions of Heaven and Earth are revealed,
and the treasure of the sage emerges.
Therefore, the yang qi (yáng qì) begins to emerge from the earth in the first month,
growing, nourishing, and lengthening above.
When its achievement is certain to be completed,
it accumulates for ten months.
Humans are also born in ten months,
conforming to the Mandate of Heaven.
Therefore, the Way of Heaven (tiān dào) is completed in ten months,
humans are also completed in ten months,
conforming to the Way of Heaven.
Therefore, the yang qi emerges from the northeast,
enters into the northwest,
arises in the first month of spring (mèng chūn),
and ends in the first month of winter (mèng dōng),
and all things invariably respond to it.
When the yang begins to emerge,
things also begin to emerge;
when the yang is at its peak,
things are also at their peak;

*Yīnyáng Chūrù Shàngxià Dìwǔshí* (陰陽出入上下第五十, The Fiftieth [Section] on *Yīn* and *Yáng* Exiting, Entering, Ascending, and Descending)
The grand principle of the Way of Heaven:
Opposite things cannot emerge together;
*yīn* and *yáng* are such.
In spring, *yáng* emerges and *yīn* enters;
in autumn, *yīn* emerges and *yáng* enters;
in summer, *yáng* is on the right and *yīn* is on the left;
in winter, *yīn* is on the right and *yáng* is on the left.
When *yīn* emerges, then *yáng* enters;
When the Yang comes out, the Yin enters;
when the Yin goes right, the Yang goes left;
when the Yin goes left, the Yang goes right.
Therefore, in spring, they both reside in the south,
in autumn, they both reside in the north,
but they do not follow the same path.
In summer, they intersect in the front,
in winter, they intersect in the back,
but they do not follow the same principle.
They run side by side without disordering each other,
they are slippery and fluid, yet each maintains its share;
this is what is meant by the intention of Heaven.
And how does one engage in this?
The way of Heaven is such:
At the beginning of great winter,
Yin and Yang each come from one direction,
and shift towards the back.
Yin comes from the east to the west,
Yang comes from the west to the east,
until the middle of the winter month,
they meet in the north,
merging into one,
which is called the winter solstice.
Separating and departing from each other,
Yin goes to the right,
Yang goes to the left.
He who goes to the left, his path is flowing;
he who goes to the right, his path is reversing.
Rebellious Qi rises to the left,
compliant Qi descends to the right,
therefore the lower part is warm and the upper part is cold.
From this, we can see that in winter, the right side of the sky is Yin and the left side is Yang,
the upper part favors the right and the lower part favors the left.
When the winter month ends,

Yin returns south and enters Xū,

As for the middle of the spring month,

Yin is in the due west,
this is called the Spring Equinox.
The Spring Equinox means Yin and Yang are equal,
therefore day and night are equal and cold and heat are balanced,
Yin diminishes daily following Yang,
Yang increases daily and becomes vast,
therefore it becomes warm and hot.
Initially obtaining the great summer month,
they meet in the south,

this is called the Summer Solstice.

Yin goes to the left.

going to the right comes from above,

below is where the left is.

"The Way of Heaven is Not Two, Chapter Fifty-One"
The constant way of heaven:
opposing things cannot arise together,
therefore it is called one.
To be single and not dual is
the operation of Heaven.
*Yīn* and *yáng*
are opposing things,
therefore one emerges or enters,
one goes right or left.
In spring, both go south;
in autumn, both go north;
in summer, they intersect in the front;
in winter, they intersect in the back.
They move in parallel but on different paths,
they converge but each manages its own affairs.
Is this their pattern?
The Way of Heaven
has one emerging and one entering,
one resting and one lurking.
Their measure is one,
yet their intentions are different.
When *yáng* emerges,
it always hangs in the front and takes on the affairs of the year;
when *yīn* emerges,
it always hangs in the back and guards emptiness.
When *yáng* rests,
its work is already accomplished above and it lurks below;
when *yīn* lurks,
it cannot approach righteousness and stays far from its place.
Heaven employs *yáng* but not *yīn*, favors virtue but not punishment,
and it is like this.
Therefore, when *yáng* emerges, it is ahead;
when *yīn* emerges, it is behind.
Thus, the intention to value virtue and despise punishment is revealed.
When *yáng* emerges, it accumulates in summer,

when *yīn* emerges, it accumulates in winter,

One must examine things with this understanding.
Heaven does not remain constant with things,

What is appropriate for the time,

Therefore, opening one thing, closing one thing, starting one thing, abolishing one thing,

"One" means singularity.

Matters are neither large nor small,

Therefore, the eye cannot see two things at once,

Drawing a square with one hand,

What governance lacks constancy?

"郊語第六十五" (Jiāo Yǔ Dì Liùshíwǔ - "Suburban Discourses, Sixty-Fifth"):
People say:

These ten things

Since things happen that are beyond what people expect,
and have already occurred,
could it be that auspiciousness, misfortune, disaster, blessing, benefit, and detriment arise from
things that are not strange,
but are beyond what people expect,
and are like this?
These are things to be feared.
Kǒngzǐ said:
"The 君子 (jūnzǐ - noble person) has three fears:
fear of 天命 (tiānmìng - the Mandate of Heaven),
They fear great men,
they fear the words of sages."
How could they not harm people,
that Kǒngzǐ (孔子) merely feared them?
From this, it can be seen that Heaven must be feared and respected,
just as the sovereign must be served with diligence.
If you do not serve your sovereign with diligence,
the calamity that comes is obviously visible.
If you do not fear and respect Heaven,
the disaster that comes is hidden.
Hidden means that one does not see the cause,
as if it were natural.
Therefore it is said:
"Vast is Heaven,
the calamity does not necessarily manifest immediately,
silent and without sound,
hidden and without form."
From this perspective,
the only difference between Heaven's calamity and the sovereign's punishment
is that one is hidden and the other is obvious.
Otherwise, when they befall people,
there is hardly any difference.
Kǒngzǐ (孔子) treated them as the same,
both saying they are to be feared.
The mind of Heaven and Earth and the spirits,
and the truth of the success or failure of human affairs,
are indeed something that no one can see,
only sages can see them.
聖人者、見人之所不見者也， The sage is one who sees what others do not see.
故聖人之言亦可畏也。 Therefore, the words of a sage are also to be feared.
奈何而廢 jiāo 禮？ How could one abolish the suburban sacrifice?
jiāo 禮者、人所最甚重也。 The suburban sacrifice is what people value most highly.
廢聖人所最甚重， To abolish what the sage valued most highly,
而吉凶利害在於冥冥不可得見之中， and good fortune, bad fortune, benefit, and harm lie in the darkness, unseen,
雖已多受其病， even though one has already suffered much from its ill effects,
何從知之？ how would one know it?
故曰： Therefore, it is said:
問聖人者， When questioning the sage,
問其所為而無問其所以為也。 ask what he does, but do not ask why he does it.
問其所以為， If you ask why he does it,
終弗能見， you will never be able to see it;
不如勿問。 it is better not to ask.
問其所為而為之， Ask what he does and do it,
所不為而勿為， what he does not do, do not do,

"Chapter 66: The Meaning of the Suburban Sacrifice"
The Meaning of the Suburban Sacrifice:
According to the laws of the *Chūnqiū* (Spring and Autumn Annals),
the king should once a year offer sacrifice to Heaven in the suburb,
and four times a year offer sacrifice in the ancestral temple.
The ancestral temple sacrifices are based on the changes of the four seasons,
the suburban sacrifice is based on the beginning of the new year.
The sages had a reason for initiating this,
and therefore the sacrifice could not be performed by anyone else but the king.
Heaven is the sovereign of all spirits,
and is the most revered by the king.
Because of this most reverent regard for Heaven,
therefore, at the beginning of each new year,
one immediately performs the suburban sacrifice at its commencement.
The suburban sacrifice must be performed on the *shàngxīn* day of the first month,
indicating that the most revered is used to commence the affairs of the year.
Every change of the calendar is marked with a suburban sacrifice.
The suburban sacrifice begins it,
prioritizing the noble,
honoring the Way of Heaven.
"Chapter 67: The Suburban Sacrifice"
According to the meaning of the *Chūnqiū*,
if a state experiences a great mourning,
the sacrifices at the ancestral temple are stopped,
And not just stopping suburban sacrifices,
they dared not abandon the rites to Heaven and Earth because of the mourning for their parents.
The mourning for one's parents
is the ultimate grief and sorrow,
yet they still dared not abandon the suburban sacrifices.
Who, then, is sufficient to abandon the suburban sacrifices?
Therefore, in the rites,
it also says:
"Those in mourning do not sacrifice,
except that sacrificing to Heaven overrides mourning, and the ceremonies are carried out."
The ancients' awe and reverence for Heaven and their emphasis on the suburban sacrifices
were exceedingly great.
Now, the assembled ministers and scholars do not investigate
and say:
"The myriad people are mostly poor,
some are somewhat hungry and cold;
is it sufficient to perform the suburban sacrifices?"
What a mistaken statement!
The Son of Heaven serves Heaven as a parent,
while descendants nourish the myriad people.
If the people are not all full,
there is no need to sacrifice to Heaven.
This is like descendants not yet having food
and therefore having no need to feed their parents.
Nothing is more contrary to reason than this.
This shows how far they have strayed from the rites.
To prioritize the noble before the lowly,
who is nobler than the Son of Heaven?
Tiānzǐ is called the Son of Heaven.
How can one accept the title of Son of Heaven
without performing the rites due to the Son of Heaven?
The Son of Heaven must not fail to sacrifice to Heaven,
just as a person must not fail to feed their father.
Therefore, the most important of the ancient sage kings'
accomplishments and writings,
was that previous kings all valued and followed these,
reverently offering the best grains,
in service to the High Heaven.
But when it came to Qín, they alone ceased and abandoned them.
How greatly did they fail to follow the old rules!
Heaven is the great sovereign of the spirits.
If the service to Heaven is incomplete,
even serving a hundred spirits will be of no avail.
How do I say this?
Sacrificing to earth deities
is criticized in the *Chūnqiū* (Spring and Autumn Annals).
Kǒngzǐ said:
"If one offends Heaven,
there is nowhere to pray."
This is the principle.
Therefore, I have not seen the state of Qín attaining heavenly blessings like the state of Zhōu.
The *Shī* (Book of Odes) says:
"Only this King Wén
was cautious and reverent,
clearly serving the Supreme God,

"Duō fú zhě," is not referring to people,
but to accomplishments and merits,
referring to what Heaven blesses.
The *Commentary* says:
"In the state of Zhōu, the royal family had many worthy individuals.

four births yielding eight boys,

This is how Heaven caused the state of Zhōu to rise;
it was not something that the state of Zhōu could accomplish on its own.
Now, both Qín and Zhōu have attained the position of Son of Heaven,
but the way they serve Heaven is different from Zhōu.
They consider the suburban sacrifice (*jiāo*) to be the beginning of all the hundred gods.
At the start of the year,
they must first offer sacrifice to Heaven on the first *xīn* day of the first month
before daring to sacrifice to Earth,
which is the principle of prioritizing the noble.
The difference between prioritizing the year and not performing it during the year
is vast.
If the blessings of Heaven seem unremarkable,
yet the reason they have not been realized for so long
is not because it is obviously correct, but they deliberately do not perform it;
rather, the officials in charge of rituals are constantly suspicious
and no one can clearly illuminate its correctness.
Now, I believe whether it is correct or not
can be determined by introspecting within one's own heart.
Yáo said to Shùn:
"The mandate of Heaven rests upon your person."
Speaking of examining oneself to understand Heaven,
nowadays one has children,
who would not want their children to observe the proper rituals for having children?
Sages rectify names,

The Son of Heaven is the son of Heaven.
Measuring Heaven by oneself,
why would one not want his son to observe the proper rituals for having children?
Now, being the Son of Heaven,

What I have heard is that:
When the world is at peace,

Now that disasters arise,

The reason the world is not yet at peace

The *Shī* (Book of Poetry) says:

"Enlightened" means evident;

*Sì Jì Dì Liùshíbā* (Chapter Sixty-Eight, "The Four Sacrifices")
In ancient times, there were four seasonal sacrifices.
These four sacrifices
were based on what was produced and ripened in the four seasons.
and were used to sacrifice to one's ancestors and parents.
Therefore, spring was called *cí*,
summer was called *yuè*,
autumn was called *cháng*,
and winter was called *zhēng*.
This means not missing the proper time
to offer sacrifices to one's ancestors.
To not sacrifice when the time is right
is to fail in the way of being a son.
*Cí* is when the eating of chives begins in the first month;
*yuè* is when the eating of wheat begins in the fourth month;
*cháng* is when the tasting of millet and sorghum begins in the seventh month;
*zhēng* is when the offering of the first rice harvest begins in the tenth month.
This is the constant order of Heaven
and the righteousness of Earth.
Filial sons and filial wives follow the seasons of Heaven
and take advantage of the benefits of Earth.
Having received the mandate to become king,
one must first sacrifice to Heaven
before carrying out royal affairs;
this is exemplified by Wén Wáng's 文王 attack on Chóng 崇.
The *Book of Poetry* says:
"Dignified is the sovereign prince,
On his left and right, they present their jade tablets.
Presenting their jade tablets in dignified manner,
Worthy officers are thus appropriate."
This refers to Wén Wáng's suburban sacrifice.

"Abundant is that Jīng River boat,

reached the beginning of the year,

*Shùn Mìng Dì Qīshí* (Chapter 70, Obedience to Destiny)
A father is the heaven of his son,
and heaven is the heaven of the father.
To be born without heaven
has never happened.
Heaven is the ancestor of all things;
all things cannot be born without heaven.
*Dú yīn* (exclusive *yīn*) cannot produce life,
*dú yáng* (exclusive *yáng*) cannot produce life;
*yīn* and *yáng* join with heaven and earth and only then is there life.
Therefore, it is said:
the son of a father is to be revered,
the son of a mother is to be humbled;
the revered takes the title of reverence,
the humbled takes the title of humility.
Therefore, those whose virtue matches heaven and earth
are aided by august heaven and are treated as its children,
and are called *Tiānzǐ* (Son of Heaven).
Next are the five ranks of nobility to honor them,
all named after states and cities.
Those who have no virtue between heaven and earth are
*zhōu* (districts), *guó* (states), *rén* (people), and *mín* (commoners);
In severe cases, they were not allowed to be connected to any city or state.
They were cut off from all their blood relatives,
separated from human relationships,
and were merely called gatekeepers and thieves.
They had no name or title in the world,
being the lowest of the low.
The respect for the highest virtue
is so towering that nothing can be added to it;
the lowness of the most base
is so dark that nothing can be below it.
The *Chūnqiū* (Spring and Autumn Annals) lists the order of ranks, displaying the arrangement of the high and low,
plainly visible and easily observed.
Even the dim-witted and foolish
cannot fail to understand it clearly.
The vegetables, gourds, and fruits of the earth,
the rice, wheat, millet, and sorghum that are cultivated,
when the vegetables grow and the grains ripen,
they always think of auspicious days,
prepare offerings and sacrificial items,
fast and cleanse themselves,
purify and reverently pay their respects,
to sacrifice to their ancestors and parents.
Filial sons and daughters-in-law do not let the proper time pass,
treat them with love and respect,
act with courtesy and humility,
and thus will likely avoid committing offenses.
Even if Gōngzǐ Qìngfù's 公子慶父 crimes were severe, they should not have implicated the state;
due to the kinship, they concealed his wrongdoing.
And the maternal uncles of the state were like Zhòngsūn of Qí,
removing the affinity of the duke.
Therefore, those who commit great crimes and do not obey the mandate of Heaven,
all abandon their natural relationships.
People depend on Heaven,
and receive the mandate through the Dao;
as for people,
they receive the mandate through words.
Those who do not conform to the Dao,
Heaven cuts them off;
those who do not conform to words,
people cut them off.
A subject receives a great mandate from the ruler,
resigns and leaves the borders,
only in the case of danger to the altars of state and the nation,
is he still allowed to speak out and solely ensure their safety,
as in the case of an alliance.
The Son of Heaven receives the mandate from Heaven,
the feudal lords receive the mandate from the Son of Heaven,
the son receives the mandate from the father,
the servants receive the mandate from the ruler,
the wife receives the mandate from the husband,
all those who receive mandates,
their superior is all Heaven,
although it can be said that the mandate is received from Heaven,
it is not simply Heaven.
If the Son of Heaven cannot uphold the mandate of Heaven,
then he is deposed and called a duke,
These are the descendants of kings.
If dukes and marquises cannot carry out the orders of the Son of Heaven,
then their titles are terminated, and they are not allowed to assume their positions.
This is exemplified by Wèi Hóu Shuò (衛侯朔).
If a son does not obey his father's commands,
then he is subject to punishment by a senior relative.
This is exemplified by the Heir Apparent Kuǎi Kuì (蒯聵) of Wèi (衛).
If a subject does not obey his lord's commands,
even if it is for good,
it is considered rebellion.
This is exemplified by Zhào Yāng (趙鞅) of Jìn (晉), who entered Jìnyáng (晉陽) in rebellion.
If a concubine does not obey her lord's commands,
then the accompanying women who arrive first take precedence.
If a wife does not obey her husband's commands,
then she is divorced,
unless the husband doesn't mention it.
It is said:
Those who do not conform to Heaven,
their sins are like this.
Kǒngzǐ (孔子) said:
"Revere the Mandate of Heaven,
revere great men,
revere the words of sages."
If one sacrifices to the altars of soil and grain, ancestral temples, mountains, rivers, and ghosts and spirits,
but not according to the proper way,
there will be no disaster or harm.
But as for sacrificing to Heaven, if the sacrifice is not accepted,
If the divination was unfavorable,
it would cause injury to the mouth of the ox,
and field mice would eat its horns.
Some would say it ate the ox,
others would say it ate and died,
others would say it ate and lived,
others would say it did not eat and died of itself,
others would change the divination and then the ox would die,

The transgression has depths, shallows, thinness, and thickness,
and the disasters have degrees of simplicity and severity,
which must not be overlooked.
It is like the anomalies of suburban sacrifices,
which change in accordance with the disaster,
responding without acting.
Seeing the unknown and natural causes of changes in all things,
is this not superior to words?
From this, one can see its awesomeness.
Who else but Heaven alone can administer complete extermination?
Subjects killing rulers,
sons killing fathers,
happened more than thirty times,
and in most cases the lower ones suffer losses.
Viewing it in this way,
who else is as awesome as the Mandate of Heaven and great men (dà rén)?
More than fifty states have perished,
all because they did not revere.
How much more so if one does not fear great men (dà rén),
If you single-mindedly execute them,
and the downfall of the ruler is what you aim for,
what day will it be before it happens?
Lǔ Xuān (魯宣) violated the words of the sages,
changed the ancient ways and altered the constant norms,
and disaster immediately arrived.
Can the words of the sages not be heeded with caution?
These three things to be feared

"Answers Regarding Suburban Sacrifices, Section Seventy-One"
Tíngwèi (廷尉) Minister Tāng (湯), risking death, says:
"Your minister Tāng (湯), acting on command,
inquired about the suburban sacrifices to the former Chancellor of Jiāoxī (膠西), Zhòng Shū (仲舒)."
Your minister Zhòng Shū (仲舒) replied:
"What I have heard is that in ancient times, among the rites of the Son of Heaven,
none was more important than the suburban sacrifices.
Suburban sacrifices were always held on the first *xīn* day of the first month,
so that they would precede all the spirits and take the foremost position.
In the *lǐ*, three years of mourning
did not allow one to forgo sacrificing to their ancestors, but they would not dare to abandon the suburban sacrifices.
Suburban sacrifices are more important than ancestral temples,
Heaven is more honored than man.
The *Wáng Zhì* (王制) says:
'The ox used for sacrificing to Heaven and Earth should be *jiǎn lì* (繭栗),
the ox used for ancestral temples should be *wò* (握),
"The ox of the guest is a foot."
This means that as virtue increases, the sacrificial animal becomes smaller.
The *Chūnqiū* (*Spring and Autumn Annals*) states:
"Lǔ sacrificed to the Duke of Zhōu,
using a white male ox."
The white color signifies purity.
"The imperial sacrificial animal is cleansed for three months."
Sacrificial animals are valued for their fatness and cleanliness,
and not for greedily pursuing their size.
Generally, the way to raise sacrificial animals
lies in ensuring they are fat and clean.
Colts and calves cannot yet handle coarse fodder;
it is best to let them feed from their mothers."
Your subject, Tāng, respectfully asks Zhòngshū:
"Lǔ sacrificing to the Duke of Zhōu with a white male ox,
is that not against ritual?"
Your subject, Zhòngshū, replies:
"It is according to ritual."
Your subject, Tāng, asks:
"The Zhōu Son of Heaven uses a red bull,
the dukes use animals without hair of a single colour (i.e. mixed colours).
The Duke of Zhōu was a duke,
how could he be allowed to use a pure animal?"
Your subject, Zhòngshū, replies:
"When King Wǔ died,
King Chéng was young,
still in swaddling clothes.
The Duke of Zhōu continued the work of Wén and Wǔ,
Accomplishing the achievements of two sages,
his virtue gradually matched Heaven and Earth,
his beneficence extended to the four seas.
Therefore, Chéng Wáng considered him virtuous and esteemed him.
The *Shī* (Book of Odes) says:
"Virtue is always rewarded."
Therefore, Chéng Wáng ordered a sacrifice to be offered to Zhōu Gōng with a white ox,
superior in that it was not the same color as the Son of Heaven,
and different from that of the various lords below.
Zhòng Shū foolishly believes this to be a ritual of repaying virtue."
Your servant Tāng asked Zhòng Shū:
"The Son of Heaven sacrifices to Heaven,
the lords sacrifice to Earth,
how is it that Lǔ has the right to sacrifice to the suburban altar?"
Your servant Zhòng Shū replied,
"Zhōu Gōng assisted Chéng Wáng,
and Chéng Wáng thereby attained sagacity,
no achievement is greater than this.
Zhōu Gōng was a sage,
and he had a sacrifice to the way of Heaven.
Therefore, Chéng Wáng ordered Lǔ to perform the suburban sacrifice."
Your servant Tāng asked Zhòng Shū:
"Lǔ sacrifices to Zhōu Gōng using a white ox,
what does it use for the suburban sacrifice?"
Your servant Zhòng Shū replied,
"Lǔ uses a pure red bull for the suburban sacrifice,
red being the color of the Zhōu,
Lǔ sacrifices to the suburban altar by order of the Son of Heaven,
Therefore, use a *xīng* (reddish-brown horse).
Your servant Tāng asked Zhòng Shū:
"When sacrificing at the ancestral temple, if one uses a *wù* (domestic duck) in place of a *fú* (wild duck, mallard),
the *wù* is not a *fú*,
is it permissible?"
Zhòng Shū replied:
"The *wù* is not a *fú*,
and the *fú* is not a *wù*.
Your servant has heard that when Kǒngzǐ entered the Grand Temple,
he asked about everything,
demonstrating the utmost caution.
Your Majesty personally examines everything,
fasts and bathes,
to serve the ancestral temple,
with utmost reverence and care.
How can you use a *fú* in place of a *wù*, or a *wù* in place of a *fú*?
If the name and reality do not correspond,
and you serve the Grand Temple in this way,
would that not be inappropriate?
Your servant Zhòng Shū, in his foolishness, believes it is not permissible.
Your servant is old and decrepit,
grant me my bones,
so I may dwell in a humble alley.
Your Majesty has deigned to have the Nine Ministers ask me about matters of the court,
but your servant is foolish and ignorant.
I am not sufficient to receive such a clear decree
and offer a weighty response.
Your servant Zhòng Shū presumes to report this at the risk of death."
Chunqiu Fanlu, Scroll 16
"Presenting Gifts" (Zhí Zhì Dì Qīshí'èr)
Concerning presenting gifts:
The Son of Heaven uses "chàng" (暢),
Dukes and marquises use jade,
High officials use lamb,
Grand Masters use geese.
The goose is similar to elders.
Elders are above the people,
and must bestow benefits with a sense of sequence and priority.
They must be virtuous and govern with order and ranks.
Therefore, Grand Masters use it as a gift.
The lamb is similar to Heaven.
The Way of Heaven
relies on Yang, not Yin;
the Way of the King
relies on Virtue, not punishments,
following Heaven.
The lamb has horns but does not use them,
possessing tools but not employing them,
resembling those who love benevolence.
Holding it, it does not cry out;
killing it, it does not complain,
resembling those who die for righteousness.
When a lamb eats from its mother,
it always kneels to receive it,
resembling those who know propriety.
Therefore, the word "sheep" is similar to the word "auspicious"!
Therefore, ministers use it as a gift.
Jade resembles a virtuous person.
The Master said:
"If a man does not say, 'What should I do? What should I do?',
I can really do nothing with him."
Therefore, one who conceals illness will not find a good doctor;
sages avoid those who are ashamed to ask questions,
considering it seeking distant merit while being close to disaster;
this is considered as having nothing.
Jade is extremely clear but does not hide its flaws;
if there are blemishes inside,
they will inevitably be seen on the outside;
therefore, a virtuous person does not conceal his shortcomings.
If one does not know, then ask;
if one is not able, then learn;
this is taken from the quality of jade.
The virtuous person compares himself to jade;
jade is smooth but not defiled,
this is benevolence and utmost purity;
it is honest but not sharp,
this is righteousness without harm;
it is firm but not brittle,
it is surpassed but not drenched.
Viewed, it appears ordinary,
displayed, it is like stone,
its appearance is like stone,
scratch it and it cannot be burned,
Pure white like plain silk, not accepting defilement,
possessing the qualities of jade,
therefore dukes and marquises use it as a gift.
*Chàng* (a fragrant substance) has similarities to a sage,
purely benevolent and genuinely refined,
and possesses the nobility of wisdom.
That which is selected from the person entirely becomes virtuous sound,
and that which is expressed in affairs entirely becomes enriching influence.
Accumulating beauty emits a fragrant aroma,
to communicate with Heaven.
*Chàng* also takes the essence of hundreds of fragrances,
uniquely blends them,
combines them into one,
and expresses their scent,
its aroma pervades Heaven.
Its pure refinement is without defect,
it is one with the sage,
therefore the Son of Heaven uses it as a gift.
And each uses them to serve their superiors.
Observing the meaning of the gift,
one can see their service.
"Ode to Mountains and Rivers, Seventy-Third"
Mountains are lofty and towering,
precipitous and majestic,
enduring and not collapsing,
resembling benevolent men and those of high ideals.
Confucius said:
"The gods of mountains and rivers are established,

tools and utensils are provided,
the crooked and the straight are joined.
The large can be used for palaces, terraces, and pavilions;
the small can be used for boats, carriages, and floating bridges.
The large is invariably suitable,
the small invariably fits.
Hold an axe and it can be chopped;
bend a sickle and it can be mowed.
The living stand,
birds and beasts lie down,
the dead enter.
It contributes greatly but does not speak;
therefore, the virtuous man draws an analogy from it.
with no diminishing;
completing its height,
with no harm;
completing its greatness,
with no loss.
Small at the top,
broad at the bottom,
long and secure,

this is the Dé (virtue/power) of the mountain.
The *Shī* (Book of Odes) says:
『Jié bǐ Nánshān,
wéi shí yán yán;
hèhè Shī Yǐn,
mín jù ěr zhān.』
Cǐ zhī wèi yě."
Water, its source, the spring gushing forth continuously,
never ceasing day or night,
is like someone strong;
filling each hollow before moving onward,
is like someone who maintains fairness;
following the slightest pathways downwards,
not neglecting the smallest space,

following streams and valleys without getting lost,

damming it and it becomes clear,

entering impure,
and exiting purified,

plunging into a chasm of a thousand *rèn* without hesitation,

all things are overcome by fire,

all gain life from it,
Losing it and dying,
is indeed like someone with virtue.
Kǒngzǐ said on the riverbank:
"Passing away is like this,
not ceasing day and night."
This is what it means.

*Stopping Rain, Chapter Seventy-Five*
If there is too much rain,
Order the counties and towns, on days associated with earth,
to block waterways and ditches,
close roads,
cover wells,
and prohibit women from entering the market.
Order the counties, townships, and villages to all sweep under the altar of the earth god (shè).
In counties and towns, if the assistant magistrate (chéng), magistrate (lì), and tax collector (sèfū) number three or more,
one priest (zhù);
in townships, if the tax collector (xiāng sèfū) and clerks number three or more,
one priest (zhù);
in villages, if the village head (lǐzhèng) and elders number three or more,
one priest (zhù);
all shall abstain for three days,
each wearing seasonal clothing.
Prepare one pig,
and sufficient millet, salt, fine wine, and other provisions,
to sacrifice to the earth god (shè).
Beat drums for three days,
and the priest (zhù) first bows twice,
then kneels and presents the offering,
having presented it,
bows twice again,
and then rises.
The priest (zhù) says:
"Alas!
Heaven produces the five grains to nourish the people,
but now there is excessive rain,
and the five grains are not in harmony.
Respectfully presenting a fat sacrificial animal and clear wine,

hoping that you will stop the rain,
remove the people's suffering,
and not allow yin to extinguish yang.
If yin extinguishes yang,
it is not in accordance with Heaven.
Heaven's constant intention
lies in benefiting the people.
The people desire the rain to stop,
and dare to announce this to the local shrines."
They drummed without singing,
and stopped only when dismissed.
In all great rites for stopping rain,
women should be hidden and concealed,
men should be harmonious and joyful,
opening yang and closing yin,
closing water and opening fire.
Use red silk to wrap around the local shrine ten times.

Stopping Rain.
The ritual for stopping rain involves
abolishing Yin and promoting Yang.
A document addresses seventeen counties,

If Yin destroys Yang,

Drums are used with sacrificial animals at the earth altar.

As soon as the writ arrives,
