"Record of Sacrifice, Number Seventy-Six"
The nature of the five grains and foods
is what Heaven uses to bestow gifts on people.
The ancestral temple honors the completion of the four seasons.
Receiving gifts and offering them in the ancestral temple
is the nature of reverence,
and it is fitting for the sacrifices.
For sacrifices in the ancestral temple,
there is no greater importance than the abundance of the offerings.
In spring, they offer *dòu shí* (bean produce).
In summer, they offer *suàn shí* (算實, sorrel produce).
In autumn, they offer *guǐ shí* (黍 produce).
In winter, they offer *dūn shí* (稻 produce).
*Dòu shí* is chives,
which are the first things to grow in spring.
*Suàn shí* is *fēng* (麷, a dish made from cooked wheat or barley),
which is the first thing received in summer.
Qiúshí is millet,
what matures first in autumn;
dūnshí is rice,
what ripens completely in winter.
Because it is first born, it is called *cí*,
to value its stewardship;
because it is simple in summer, it is called *yuē*,
to value what is initially offered.
Because it matures first, it is called *cháng*,
*cháng* speaks of sweetness;
because it is completely ripe, it is called *zhēng*,
*zhēng* speaks of abundance.
Offering up what is received from Heaven in the four seasons,
is called the *shàng jì* (highest sacrifice),
valuing the bounty of Heaven,
and also honoring the ancestral temple.
Kǒngzǐ would use what he received as a gift from the ruler to make sacrifices,
how much more so would he do with what he received as a gift from Heaven?
Within one year,
Heaven's bounty arrives four times,
and when it arrives, it is offered up,
this is why the ancestral temple has four seasonal sacrifices per year.
Therefore, the *jūnzǐ* never fails to eat new produce;
when new bounty from Heaven arrives,
he must first offer it,
then take it to eat,
showing reverence for Heaven and respect for the ancestral temple.
Reverence for Heaven is a beautiful virtue,
Paying reverence to ancestral temples is a great ritual.
It is what the sages carefully attend to.
One does not seek abundance but desires purity and cleanliness,
one does not covet large numbers but desires reverence and respect.
When a *jūnzǐ* offers sacrifice,
he reverently approaches it himself,
expressing the sincerity of his heart,
exhausting the way of reverence and purity,
in order to connect with the utmost honored.
Therefore, the spirits enjoy it.
When the spirits enjoy it in this way,
only then can one be said to be able to perform a sacrifice.
*Jì* (祭, sacrifice) means *chá* (察, to observe, examine);
it means to successfully reach the spirits.
To successfully reach those who cannot be heard or seen,
therefore it is called *chá* (察, to observe, examine).
I enjoy [the offering] in accordance with the name [of the spirit];
therefore, the sacrifice is not in vain.
How can one observe it?
*Jì* (祭, sacrifice) means *jì* (際, boundary, juncture).
Only by participating in the sacrifice can one see the unseen.
Seeing the unseen,
only then does one understand the Mandate of Heaven and the spirits.
Understanding the Mandate of Heaven and the spirits,
only then does one understand the meaning of sacrifice.
Understanding the meaning of sacrifice,
one then knows to value sacrificial matters.
Kǒngzǐ 孔子 said:
"If I do not participate in the sacrifice,
then sacrificing to the spirits is as if the spirits are truly present."
Value sacrificial matters,
as if they were matters of life and death.
Therefore, the sage, concerning ghosts and spirits,
reveres them and dares not deceive them,
believes in them but does not rely on them solely,
serves them but does not depend on them entirely.
Rely on their impartiality,
to reward those who have virtue;
hope that they are not selfish,
to bestow blessings on people.
As it is seen in the *Shī* (Book of Poetry), it says:
"Alas, you gentlemen,
do not constantly rest in ease.
Quietly attend to your positions,
cherish this integrity and uprightness.
The spirits will listen to you,
and grant you great blessings."
Those who are upright obtain blessings,
those who are not upright do not obtain blessings,
this is the law of it.
The *Shī* is taken as the law of the world.
How can it be said to be not the law?
Its words are direct and weighty,
and there are repeated exclamations,
wanting people to understand its meaning.
Yet people still do not understand,
How forgotten it is!
Kǒngzǐ said:
"The weight of the writings,
the repetition of the words.
Alas!
It must be examined closely.
There must be something beautiful within it."
This is what it means.
"Following the Way of Heaven, Seventy-seventh"
Following the way of Heaven,
to nourish one's self,
is called the Dao.
Heaven has two harmonies to create two centers,
the year establishes its center within them,
its use is inexhaustible.
The center of the North uses and combines with yin,
and things begin to move below;
the center of the South uses and combines with yang,
and nourishment begins to flourish above.
That which moves below,
cannot come to life without the harmony of the East,
this is mid-spring.
That which is nourished above,
cannot come to completion without the harmony of the West,
this is mid-autumn.
Thus, the beauty and ugliness of Heaven and Earth,
lies in the place of the two harmonies,
The place where the two extremes return to is where they accomplish their being.
Therefore, harmony: the East gives rise to it and the West completes it.
In the East, harmony arises,
and the North is where it initially originates;
and in the West, harmony is completed,
and the South is where it is nurtured and grows.
Its origination
does not extend to where harmony cannot give rise to it;
Its nurturing and growth do not extend to where harmony cannot complete it.
Completion lies in harmony;
birth must be harmonious.
Begin in the center;
stop in the center.
The center is where all under Heaven ends and begins;
and harmony
is what Heaven and Earth generate and complete.
Indeed, no virtue is greater than harmony,
and no way is more correct than the center.
The center is the beautiful, thorough principle of Heaven and Earth,
what the sages preserve.
The *Classic of Poetry* says:
“Neither too firm nor too yielding,
spreading governance with ease.”
Is this not the meaning of moderation and harmony?
Therefore, those who can govern the world with moderation and harmony
their virtue will be greatly abundant;
those who can nourish their bodies with moderation and harmony,
their lifespan will reach the limit of their destiny.
The laws of men and women,
are the laws of Yin and Yang.
Yang *qì* arises from the north,
reaches its peak in the south,
and having peaked, unites with Yin.
Yin *qì* arises from the central summer,
reaches its peak in the central winter,
and having peaked, unites with Yang.
If it does not peak, it does not unite.
Therefore, in the tenth month they are both at their peak together,
and by the end of the year, they unite again.
Heaven and earth follow this pattern for a long time,
taking this as the norm.
Therefore, first follow these internal laws,
nurture the body to preserve it completely,
so that men are firm and potent and capable of maintaining a household,
and Yin does not reach its peak without interaction.
Therefore, the body's essence is clear,
difficult to weaken and firm,
long-lived and without error.
This is the Way of Heaven and Earth.
The *qì* of Heaven first strengthens the male before releasing essence,
therefore its essence is solid.
The *qì* of Earth first strengthens the female before transforming,
therefore its transformations are good.
Therefore, the meeting of Yin and Yang,
unites with the north in winter, and things move below;
unites with the south in summer, and things move above.
Great movements above and below,
all occur after the solstices.
When it is cold, the ice congeals and the ground cracks;
when it is hot, the sand is scorched and the rocks rot.
The essence of the *qì* arrives at this point.
Therefore, the transformations of Heaven and Earth:
the spring *qì* generates, and all things emerge;
the summer *qì* nurtures, and all things grow;
the autumn *qì* kills, and all things die;
the winter *qì* collects, and all things are stored.
Therefore, only the *qì* of Heaven and Earth is refined,
entering and exiting without form,
and all things invariably respond;
this is the ultimate actuality.
The *jūnzǐ* models what they deem valuable.
The Yin and Yang of Heaven and Earth correspond to male and female,
the male and female of humans correspond to Yin and Yang.
Yin and Yang can also be called male and female,
male and female can also be called Yin and Yang.
The standard of Heaven and Earth,
reaches the middle of the east,
where what is produced is greatly nurtured;
reaches the middle of the west,
where what is nurtured is greatly completed.
One year starts four times,
and its business must rely on the center.
What the center does,
must rely on harmony;
Therefore, it is said that harmony is essential.
Harmony is the correctness of Heaven,
the equilibrium of Yin and Yang.
Its Qi is the most excellent,
the origin of all things.
If one sincerely chooses harmony,
it is considered a great reception of the offerings of Heaven and Earth.
The Dao of Heaven and Earth,
even if there are instances of disharmony,
inevitably returns to harmony,
and what is done will be meritorious.
Even if there are instances of immoderation,
it inevitably ceases at moderation,
and what is done will not be lost.
Therefore, the movement of Yang
begins in the center of the North
and ends in the center of the South.
The movement of Yin
begins in the center of the South
and ends in the center of the North.
The Dao of Yin and Yang is different,
but when it reaches its peak, it all ceases at the center.
The place where they both begin must be in the center.
The center is the great ultimate of Heaven and Earth,
the place where the sun and moon reach and then retreat.
The waxing and waning of length
must not exceed the center;
it is the rule of Heaven and Earth.
Combining harmony and disharmony,
centering and non-centering,
and applying them according to the time,
exhaustively making them into accomplishment.
Therefore, there is no time that is not timely;
this is the Way of Heaven and Earth.
Following the Way of Heaven,
moderation is the regulation of Heaven;
yang is the generosity of Heaven;
yin is the urgency of Heaven;
centering is the application of Heaven;
harmony is the accomplishment of Heaven.
Taking up the Way of Heaven and Earth,
and finding beauty in harmony,
therefore, when things are born,
they all value qi and welcome its nourishment.
Mèngzǐ said:
"I am good at nourishing my vast and flowing qi."
This means that conduct must always adhere to ritual,
and the heart is naturally joyful,
constantly using yang to attain the birth of its intention.
Gōngsūn's method of nourishing qi says:
"If the inside is stored too full, then qi will not flow;
if too empty, then qi will be insufficient;
if heat prevails, then qi will [□];
if cold prevails, then qi will [□];
if too much labor, then qi will not enter;
if too much leisure, then qi will arrive languidly;
When angry, the *qì* rises;
when happy, the *qì* scatters;
when worried, the *qì* becomes disordered;
when afraid, the *qì* is subdued.
All ten of these,
are harms to the *qì*,
and all arise from not being centered and harmonious.
Therefore, when a *jūnzǐ* is angry, they return to the center,
and pacify themselves with harmony;
when happy, they return to the center,
and restrain it with uprightness;
when worried, they return to the center,
and relax it with intention;
when afraid, they return to the center,
and solidify it with essence."
Thus, the necessity of returning to centering and harmony is like this.
Therefore, when the *jūnzǐ*'s *dào* is achieved,
the *qì* flourishes and ascends.
All *qì* follows the heart/mind.
The heart/mind is the ruler of the *qì*,
how could the *qì* not follow it?
Therefore, those who understand the *dào* of the world,
all say that nurturing the inner heart/mind is its foundation.
Therefore, the reason why people of *rén* live long lives is
that externally they have no greed, and internally they are pure and tranquil,
their hearts/minds are peaceful and do not lose centeredness and correctness,
they take the beauty of Heaven and Earth to nourish their bodies,
and this is how they live long and healthily.
The reason why the crane lives long is that
it harbors no stagnant Qi within.
Therefore, it eats ice.
The reason why the ape lives long is that
it likes to stretch its limbs.
Therefore, its Qi spreads in all directions.
The Qi of Heaven constantly bestows downwards upon the Earth.
Therefore, the follower of the Dao also draws Qi to the feet.
The Qi of Heaven is always moving and does not stagnate.
Therefore, the follower of the Dao also does not harbor stagnant Qi.
If one does not regulate,
even when full, one is not truly replete.
Therefore, the superior man nurtures and harmonizes it,
moderates and models it,
removes its excessive comfort,
takes its harmonious multitude.
High terraces have too much Yang,
spacious rooms have too much Yin,
far removed from the harmony of Heaven and Earth.
Therefore, the sage does not do them,
but finds what is suitable in the middle way.
The standard for man is eight chi (尺),
four chi (尺) is the middle.
The "Gōng" (宮) note is the central sound,
the sweet taste is the central flavor,
four chi (尺) is the central measure.
Therefore, the rites of the Three Kings,
in taste, all valued sweetness,
Shēng jiē shàng hé. All sounds value harmony.
Chǔ qí shēn suǒyǐ cháng zì jiàn yú tiāndì zhī dào, Being in one's body means constantly immersing oneself in the Way of Heaven and Earth,
qí dào tónglèi, its Way being of the same kind,
yī qì zhī biàn yě. is a differentiation of the one Qi.
Fǎ tiān zhě, nǎi fǎ rén zhī biàn. To model oneself on Heaven is to differentiate oneself through modeling on others.
Tiān zhī dào, The Way of Heaven
xiàng qiū dōng ér yīn lái, tends towards autumn and winter, and the Yin comes,
xiàng chūn xià ér yīn qù. tends towards spring and summer, and the Yin departs.
Shìgù gǔ zhī rén shuāng jiàng ér yíng nǚ, Therefore, in ancient times, when the frost descended, they welcomed women,
bīng pàn ér shā nèi, when the ice melted, they diminished [sexual activity] within,
yǔ yīn jù jìn, being close to the Yin,
yǔ yáng jù yuǎn yě. and far from the Yang.
Tiāndì zhī qì, The Qi of Heaven and Earth
bù zhì shèng mǎn, does not reach its peak fullness,
bù jiāo yīnyáng. and does not intermingle Yin and Yang.
Shìgù jūnzǐ shén ài qì ér yóu yú fáng, Therefore, the gentleman deeply cherishes Qi and moves through the rooms [of the house],
yǐ tǐ tiān yě. in order to embody Heaven.
Qì bù shāng yú yǐ shèng tōng, Qi is not harmed by its abundance and flow,
ér shāng yú bùshí, tiān bìng. but is harmed by being untimely and violating Heaven.
Bù yǔ yīnyáng jù wǎnglái, Not going and coming together with Yin and Yang
wèi zhī bùshí; is called untimely;
zì qí yù ér bù gù tiānshù, indulging desires without regard for the numbers of Heaven
wèi zhī tiān bìng. is called violating Heaven.
Jūnzǐ zhì shēn, The gentleman governs his body,
bù gǎn wéi tiān. daring not violate Heaven.
Shìgù xīn mǔ shírì ér yī yóu yú fáng, Therefore, a new male [i.e., a young man] should engage in sexual activity once every ten days,
zhōngnián zhě bèi xīn mǔ, a middle-aged man, double that of a new male,
shǐ shuāi zhě bèi zhōngnián, a man in the early stages of decline, double that of a middle-aged man,
The state of being moderately weakened increases when the initial decline begins;
a greatly weakened state occurs when the new male (新牡, xīn mǔ) appears like the new moon,
and becomes synchronized with the rhythm of Heaven and Earth.
This is a rough outline of the principle.
However, the key points all aim at avoiding extreme prosperity and avoiding clashes.
Sparseness in spring and spaciousness in summer
means not straying far from the numbers of Heaven and Earth.
People all know to cherish their clothing and food,
but do not cherish their Heavenly Qi (天氣, tiān qì).
The Heavenly Qi (天氣, tiān qì) to people
is more important than clothing and food.
If clothing and food are exhausted,
there is still some time left,
but when the Qi (氣, qì) is exhausted, life ends immediately.
Therefore, the greatest principle of nourishing life
lies in cherishing Qi (氣, qì).
Qi (氣, qì) is formed from the spirit (神, shén),
and the spirit (神, shén) emanates from the intent (意, yì).
What the heart directs is called intent (意, yì);
when the intent (意, yì) is labored, the spirit (神, shén) is disturbed,
and when the spirit (神, shén) is disturbed, the Qi (氣, qì) is diminished.
When the Qi (氣, qì) is diminished, it is difficult to live long.
Therefore, a virtuous person restrains desires and stops evil to pacify the intent (意, yì),
pacifies the intent (意, yì) to quiet the spirit (神, shén),
and quiets the spirit (神, shén) to nourish the Qi (氣, qì).
When the Qi (氣, qì) is abundant and ordered,
then the greatest principle of nourishing the body is attained.
An ancient Daoist (道士, Dàoshì) said:
"If you wish to have no encroachment,
firmly adhere to one virtue."
This means if the spirit does not leave the body,
then the *qì* will be abundantly internally filled,
and one can endure hunger and cold.
Harmony and joy are external comfort in life;
spiritual vigor is internal fullness in life;
external comfort is not as good as internal fullness,
much less external injury?
Anger, grief, worry, and resentment
are injuries to life;
harmony, pleasure, exhortation, and goodness
are nourishment for life.
The *jūnzǐ* is cautious about small things and will not suffer great defeats;
acting with rectitude,
his reputation and influence will flourish;
with peaceful *qì* and intention,
and dwelling in tranquility and joy,
this can be called nurturing life.
In general, those who nurture life
value nothing more than *qì*.
Therefore, the lords of the world,
this thing alone dies.
For those that can be eaten,
tell of their taste being beneficial to people;
for those that cannot be eaten,
tell of killing, cleaning, and removing harm without waiting for autumn.
At the time when things greatly wither,
When all things die,
this thing alone lives.
Those that can be eaten,
eat them more.
Heaven benefits people because of this,
and brings them forth to live uniquely.
Those that cannot be eaten,
raise them more.
Heaven pities the area within the Zhōu (州) and Huá (華) regions,
therefore it produces *sù mài* (宿麥, winter wheat),
which ripens in the middle of the year.
The *jūnzǐ* (君子, noble person) observes the differences among things,
in order to seek the will of Heaven,
and great principles can be seen.
Therefore, men and women should take their prime,
and select the best of scents and tastes.
In dwelling, seek harmony,
and moderate labor and leisure.
In cold and warmth, do not miss what is suitable.
In hunger and fullness, do not exceed what is balanced.
Desire and aversion should be measured by reason,
and movement and stillness should follow one's nature and destiny.
Joy and anger should stop at the middle,
and worry and fear should be reversed to what is correct.
When this balance is always present in one's body,
it is called greatly obtaining the peace of Heaven and Earth.
Those who greatly obtain the peace of Heaven and Earth,
their lives are extended and lengthened.
Those who do not attain the peace of Tiāndì (天地, Heaven and Earth),
their lifespan is harmed and shortened.
The inherent nature of short and long life,
is what people receive from Heaven.
Therefore, lifespans are short or long,
nourishment is successful or unsuccessful,
and when it comes to the end,
generally speaking, it will inevitably be repaid (chóu 讎),
and no one can escape from this.
Therefore, the meaning of "shòu" (壽, longevity) is like repayment (chóu 讎).
Although the people under Heaven are numerous,
they inevitably must each repay (chóu 讎) what they have been given in life,
and their lifespan (yāo 夭, premature death) depends on their own actions.
Those who follow a path of prolonged self-conduct,
their lifespan will be repaid (chóu 讎) with longevity;
those who follow a path of unsustainable self-conduct,
their lifespan will also be repaid (chóu 讎) with brevity.
The circumstances of long and short life,
each repay (chóu 讎) according to their conduct throughout life.
Like the arrival of what is due later,
it cannot be overcome.
Therefore, it is said:
Longevity (shòu 壽) is repayment (chóu 讎).
Thus, the self-conduct of a person,
either benefits or harms their lifespan.
Those whose self-conduct is easeful and whose lifespan is long,
fate has benefited them;
those whose self-conduct is upright but whose lifespan is short,
It is fate that causes diminution.
To use what Heaven has diminished or augmented in fate
to suspect what people have gained or lost
is a great delusion.
Therefore, if Heaven increases it, but people harm it,
its increase is diminished;
if Heaven shortens it, but people nurture it,
its shortness is augmented.
Those who are prematurely diminished all do so because of people,
are people not the successors of Heaven?
If it issues its essence but people do not continue (nurture) it,
how can it stand alone?
*Luxuriant Dew of the Spring and Autumn Annals*, Scroll Seventeen
"The Conduct of Heaven and Earth, Seventy-eighth"
The conduct of Heaven and Earth is beautiful.
Therefore, in spring, wear light clothing,
in summer, dwell in dense shade,
in autumn, avoid killing winds,
in winter, avoid heavy dampness,
and accord with its harmony.
Clothing should always be washed,
food should always induce hunger.
The body should always be labored,
and there should be no long periods of ease
in abundance.
All things of Heaven and Earth
are born by taking advantage of their prosperity,
To be overcome by what it overcomes and die is the cycle of the four seasons.
This is the change of the four seasons.
Thus, the water energy of winter
is added eastward to spring, and wood is born,
riding on its flourishing.
The growth of spring
goes west to metal and dies,
overcome by what overcomes it.
What is born of wood
dies when it reaches metal;
what is born of metal
dies when it reaches fire.
What is born in spring cannot exceed autumn,
what is born in autumn cannot exceed summer;
this is the way of Heaven.
With regards to food and drink, and their odors and flavors,
each time it reaches a season,
there are things that it overcomes,
and things that it does not overcome;
these principles cannot but be observed.
The four seasons have different energies;
each energy has what is suitable for it.
Where suitability lies,
things alternately flourish.
Observe what alternately flourishes and alternately nourish with it;
those that flourish at the same time, eat them together.
These are all what is suitable.
Therefore, shepherd's purse is best in winter,
and mustard completes its growth in summer.
From this, one can see what is suitable to consume in winter and summer.
Winter is water energy,
shepherd's purse is a sweet flavor;
what flourishes by riding on water energy,
is sweetness overcoming cold.
The meaning of *jì* (薺, shepherd's purse) is “to aid,”
akin to aiding in crossing a great river.
Summer pertains to the *huǒ qì* (fire energy),
mustard has a bitter taste.
That which thrives on the *huǒ qì* and is considered good
is because bitterness overcomes heat.
Heaven speaks no words,
but conveys its intent through objects.
Objects that do not live and die at the same time as other objects
must be deeply investigated;
this is how Heaven informs people.
Therefore, the maturing of shepherd's purse indicates sweetness,
and the maturing of mustard indicates bitterness.
The gentleman observes objects and diligently adheres to the indications of their maturing.
Thus, when the time arrives that shepherd's purse is no longer edible,
he completely avoids sweet foods,
until the time that mustard matures.
That which Heaven uniquely brings to maturity,
the gentleman uniquely values;
this is what is appropriate for winter and summer.
Spring and autumn mix things for harmony,
while winter and summer alternate what is appropriate.
Then one will obtain the beauty of Heaven and Earth,
and the four seasons will be harmonious.
Generally speaking, the grand principle of selecting flavors
is to rely on what is beautiful in each season,
and thus not stray far from the way of Heaven.
Therefore, when the myriad things flourish greatly,
all creatures come to life,
and face difficulties,
without hesitating to risk their lives,
this is how to alleviate poverty.
Promoting glory,
and praising goodness,
is how to assist illumination.
Receiving orders and proclaiming grace,
assisting in the accomplishment of the *jūnzǐ* (gentleman),
is how to aid in transformation.
When achievement is accomplished and the task is completed,
attributing merit to the ruler,
is how to attain righteousness.
Therefore, the land that understands its principles is the mother of all things;
a minister who understands his duties is the steward of a country.
The mother cannot be without trustworthiness,
and the steward cannot be without loyalty.
If the mother is not trustworthy, then the grass and trees will harm their roots;
if the steward is not loyal, then treacherous ministers will endanger the ruler.
If the roots are harmed, then the branches and leaves will perish;
if the ruler is endangered, then the state will perish.
Therefore, those who act as the land strive to reveal its form,
As a minister, one must strive to make one's feelings evident.
The ruler of a state is like the heart of a body.
Dwelling in the deep palace is like the heart being hidden in the chest;
Being supremely noble and without equal is like the spirit of the heart being unique and unparalleled.
Employing officials and valuing scholars is like valuing the eyes and despising the feet.
Entrusting various officials without favoritism is like the limbs each having their own function.
Having four advisors internally is like the heart having the liver, lungs, spleen, and kidneys.
Having hundreds of officials externally is like the heart having form, body, and orifices.
Befriending sages and drawing near to the wise is like spirits and brilliance gathering in the heart.
Those above and below following each other smoothly is like the limbs acting as each other's servants.
Dispensing kindness and bestowing favor is like the primordial Qi flowing through the skin, hair, and pores.
When the common people all get what they need, it is like when the blood and Qi are harmonious and the body experiences no suffering.
Achieving great peace through non-action (wúwéi) is like the spirit and Qi naturally communicating with the abyss.
Attracting yellow dragons and phoenixes is like the spirit and brilliance attracting jade maidens and lingzhi mushrooms.
It is akin to presenting a phoenix to the Yellow Emperor,
or like deities offering jade maidens and auspicious fungi.
When the ruler is wise,
the subjects benefit from his accomplishments,
like the spirit in the heart,
allowing the body to be whole.
When the subject is virtuous,
the ruler receives his favor,
like the body being still while the heart finds peace.
When the ruler is in turmoil,
those below suffer the consequences,
like the ears and eyes being impaired, causing harm to the hands and feet.
When the subject is disloyal, the ruler meets his downfall,
like the body moving erratically, leading to the demise of the heart.
Therefore, the proper relationship between ruler and subject
is like the heart and the body.
The heart cannot be weak,
and the ruler cannot be unwise.
The body cannot be disobedient,
and the subject cannot be disloyal.
The heart's wholeness
relies on the body's strength;
the ruler's peace
relies on the subject's merit.
Therefore, Heaven holds its position high but bestows its blessings below,
conceals its form but reveals its light,
arranges the stars and draws near to the essence,
ǎo yīnyáng ér jiàng shuānglù.
Elevating his position,
is how he becomes honored;
extending his beneficence downwards,
is how he practices benevolence;
concealing his form,
is how he embodies divinity;
revealing his light,
is how he embodies clarity;
ordering the stars,
is how things succeed each other;
approaching utmost purity,
is how he embodies strength;
examining yīnyáng,
is how he completes the year;
causing frost and dew to descend,
is how he brings forth life and death.
The way of being a ruler,
its methods take their pattern from Heaven,
therefore valuing noble titles and employing ministers of the state,
is how he practices benevolence;
dwelling deeply in secluded places,
not showing his form,
is how he embodies divinity;
entrusting the worthy and employing the capable,
observing and listening to all directions,
is how he embodies clarity;
measuring abilities and assigning offices,
The wise and the foolish have differences,
and that is how they are inherited from one another;
attracting the wise from nearby
to prepare your arms and legs (capable officials),
that is how one becomes strong;
examining real achievements,
ordering merit and demerit,
that is how one succeeds in the world;
those with merit are promoted,
those without merit are demoted,
that is how rewards and punishments are handled.
Therefore, Heaven holds to its Way as the master of all things,
and the ruler holds to constancy as the master of a state.
Heaven cannot be without firmness,
and the ruler cannot be without steadfastness.
If Heaven is not firm, then the stars will disrupt their courses;
if the ruler is not steadfast, then wicked ministers will disrupt their offices.
If the stars are disrupted, then Heaven will be lost;
if the ministers are disruptive, then the ruler will be lost.
Therefore, one who acts as Heaven must strive to make its qi (vital energy) firm,
and one who acts as ruler must strive to make his government steadfast;
only with firmness and steadfastness can the way of Yang control fate.
The Earth lowers its position but raises its qi (vital energy),
exposes its form but reveals its essence,
receives its death but offers its life,
accomplishes its tasks but returns its merit.
Lowering its position,
is how it serves Heaven;
To ascend its breath [qì] is
how to nourish the *yáng*;
to expose its form is
how to achieve loyalty;
to reveal its emotions is
how to achieve trustworthiness;
to accept its death is
how to properly conceal the end;
to dedicate its life is
how to assist in enlightenment;
to accomplish its affairs is
how to aid in transformation;
to return its merit is
how to realize righteousness.
The way for one to be a minister
takes its model from the earth.
Therefore, morning and evening, advancing and withdrawing,
performing duties and responding,
is how to serve the noble;
providing food and drink,
attending to sickness and disease,
is how to provide nourishment;
entrusting oneself and giving up one's life,
not acting with exclusive control,
is how to achieve loyalty;
exhausting foolishness and expressing feelings,
not embellishing one's faults,
is how to achieve trustworthiness;
To submit to principle and die for righteousness.
It alternates through the four seasons.
And it is the governing principle of people.
How can one find a reason to delay what should be done,
and necessarily wait for the four seasons?
This is called obstruction,
and is not in accordance with the natural order.
People have joy, anger, sorrow, and pleasure,
just as heaven has spring, autumn, winter, and summer.
The arrival of joy, anger, sorrow, and pleasure at their proper time and their desire to be expressed,
is like the arrival of spring, autumn, winter, and summer at their proper time and their desire to emerge;
all are the natural workings of the celestial forces.
It is proper that they proceed directly and without stagnation,
they are one and the same.
Heaven completes one cycle of these four throughout the year,
while the ruler of men, in one day, unknowingly surpasses this number of four;
therefore, their principles cannot be considered equivalent.
Moreover, heaven's desire to benefit people
is not the same as its desire to benefit grains.
Removing impurities does not wait for a specific time,
how much less should one wait when dealing with impure people!
A "Sū Yú Version: The Movement of Heaven and Earth, Seventy-eighth"
The movement of Heaven and Earth is beautiful.
Therefore, heaven elevates its position and lowers its influence,
hides its form and reveals its light,
orders the stars in succession and draws near to the purest essence,
(Heaven) examines Yin and Yang and causes frost and dew to descend.
Exalting its position is how it is revered,
distributing its beneficence is how it is benevolent,
concealing its form is how it is divine,
revealing its light is how it is bright,
arranging the stars in order is how they succeed each other,
drawing close to perfect essence is how it is firm,
examining Yin and Yang is how the year is completed,
causing frost and dew to descend is how it generates and kills.
Those who are rulers of men,
their laws take their image from Heaven.
Therefore, valuing rank and employing the state,
is how to be benevolent;
dwelling in seclusion,
not showing one's body,
is how to be divine;
employing the worthy and using the capable,
observing and listening to all directions,
is how to be bright;
measuring ability and assigning offices,
with differences between the worthy and the foolish,
is how to succeed each other;
drawing the worthy near oneself,
to prepare arms and sinews,
is how to be firm;
examining real achievements,
ordering successes and failures,
is how to complete the age;
Those who have merit are advanced,
those who have no merit are retired.
This is the means of reward and punishment.
Therefore, Heaven upholds its Dao to be the master of all things;
the ruler upholds his constancy to be the master of one state.
Heaven cannot be without strength (gāng),
the ruler cannot be without firmness (jiān).
If Heaven is not strong, then the stars will乱 (luàn) their courses;
if the ruler is not firm, then wicked ministers will乱 (luàn) their offices.
If the stars are乱 (luàn), then their heaven will be lost;
if the ministers are乱 (luàn), then their ruler will be lost.
Therefore, he who acts as Heaven must strive to strengthen his Qi;
he who acts as ruler must strive to solidify his government;
only with strength and firmness can the Yang Dao control fate.
The earth humbles its position but elevates its Qi,
exposes its form but reveals its feelings,
accepts its death but offers its life,
completes its tasks but returns its merit.
Humbled position is the way to serve Heaven,
elevated Qi is the way to nourish Yang,
exposed form is the way to be loyal,
revealed feelings are the way to be trustworthy,
accepted death is the way to conceal the end,
offered life is the way to assist in enlightenment (míng),
completed tasks are the way to assist in transformation (huà),
returned merit is the way to achieve righteousness (yì).
Those who are ministers,
their model is taken from the earth.
Therefore, in morning and evening advance and retreat.
Serving in one's office and responding to inquiries,
is how one serves one's superior.
Providing provisions and drink,
attending to and observing illnesses,
is how one provides nourishment.
Entrusting oneself and dedicating one's life,
not acting with exclusive authority in matters,
is how one achieves loyalty.
Exhausting one's foolishness and expressing one's feelings,
not concealing one's faults,
is how one achieves trustworthiness.
Submitting one's integrity and dying in hardship,
not cherishing one's life,
is how one rescues from adversity.
Promoting and advancing glory,
praising and extolling their goodness,
is how one assists enlightenment.
Receiving orders and proclaiming grace,
assisting in the accomplishment of a virtuous person,
is how one assists in transformation.
When merit is achieved and affairs are accomplished,
attributing the virtue to the superior,
is how one achieves righteousness.
Therefore, the earth being clear in its principles is the mother of all things.
A minister being clear in his duty is the steward of a country.
A mother cannot be untrustworthy,
a steward cannot be disloyal.
If the mother does not trust, then the grass and trees will damage their roots.
If the prime minister is not loyal, then treacherous ministers will endanger their ruler.
If the roots are damaged, then the branches and leaves will be lost.
If the ruler is endangered, then the country will be lost.
Therefore, those who govern the land must make their form manifest.
Those who serve as ministers must make their feelings clear.
The ruler of a country,
is like the heart of a body.
Dwelling in the deep palace,
is like the heart hidden in the chest.
Being supremely noble and without equal,
is like the spirit of the heart, without a double.
Employing officials and superior scholars,
valuing those with high clarity and devaluing those with heavy turbidity,
is like the body valuing the eyes and devaluing the feet.
Employing many ministers without favoritism,
is like the four limbs each having their own duties.
Internally having four assistants,
is like the heart having the liver, lungs, spleen, and kidneys.
Externally having hundreds of officials,
is like the heart having form, body, openings, and orifices.
Being close to sages and near to the wise,
is like all the divine spirits gathering in the heart.
Those above and below support and obey each other,
is like the limbs serving each other.
Spreading kindness and bestowing favor,
is like the primordial energy flowing through the skin, hair, and pores.
The common people all obtain their proper place,
like when the blood and breath are harmonious,
and the physical body has no suffering.
Achieving great peace through non-action [wú wéi]
is like the spirit naturally communicating with the deep.
Attracting yellow dragons and phoenixes [huáng lóng fèng huáng]
is like the spirits attracting jade maidens and magic fungus.
If the ruler is wise,
the ministers receive the benefit of his accomplishments,
like the spirit of the heart
allowing the body to be complete.
If the ministers are virtuous,
the ruler receives the benefit of their kindness,
like the body being still while the heart obtains peace.
If the ruler is in chaos, those below suffer the consequences,
like if the ears and eyes are not clear and the hands and feet are wounded.
If the ministers are not loyal, the ruler will be destroyed,
like the body moving recklessly while the heart suffers loss because of it.
Therefore, the proper relationship between ruler and minister
is like the relationship between the heart and the body.
The heart cannot be without resolve,
and the ruler cannot be without virtue.
The body cannot be without obedience,
and the minister cannot be without loyalty.
That which allows the heart to be complete
is the strength of the body;
that which allows the ruler to be at peace
is the accomplishment of the ministers.
*Chapter 79: What Power and Virtue Produce* [Wēi Dé Suǒ Shēng Dì Qīshíjiǔ]
Heaven has harmony and virtue,
has fairness and authority,
has the principle of mutual reception,
and has the reason for governing.
